ground_truth.title: Sneak Peek: What’s Inside “Economics-Based Personal Finance”
ground_truth.author: Robert Puelz
ground_truth.main_content:
Ever wondered how economists approach the everyday money questions that shape our lives?

Fact is, I have the same money questions as you. My education and experience have afforded me a front-row seat over the last fifteen years to see how better personal finance decisions are made. Short version: conventional wisdom has been fine-tuned by knowledge and tech.

I’m including the table of contents for our new book to help you spot chapters that speak to your needs or curiosity. Chapters cover topics like maximizing your living standard, making smarter decisions about investing and retirement, evaluating risk, and much more.

From “Human Capital” and “Consumption Smoothing” to practical case studies on choosing where to live or building your portfolio, this book pulls together Nobel Laureate ideas and real-world tools like MaxiFi Planner to help readers see personal finance through a fresh, simple lens.

I’m here on Substack to help you make better money choices. The book is part of the deal.

Hit reply if there is a section of a chapter you’d be especially excited to read, and I’ll share the current draft with you. If there’s a personal finance topic that’s particularly relevant to you, let me know. I want this work to pinpoint the needs and interests of my Substack readers.

The complete book is available exclusively to paid subscribers.

Chapter 1 of the 2026 edition is dropping in their Inbox on Friday.

The TOC is attached.

Have a great rest of your week!
